verdict.line: You lose if you walk into Blinding Dart range to farm and get poked for free; you win if you let his Q go on cooldown before you commit, since the matchup sits at 50.5% over 95 games with the solo-kill edge on your side.

brief.thesis: Teemo's only real defense is Q (Blinding Dart), an 8-second-cooldown blind that nullifies your attack damage — including Q (Knuckle Down)'s empowered punches — but does nothing to W (Haymaker), which deals its true/physical damage directly rather than as an attack. The entire lane is a cooldown-tracking exercise: trade when his dart is down, absorb poke with stored Grit when it's up.

theirWindow.when: His Q is up, yours is on cooldown
theirWindow.what: He can blind your attacks and poke freely with Toxic Shot (E, 0 cooldown, applies on every auto) without any risk of a clean trade back. Back off and let your Haymaker Grit build off the chip damage instead of forcing a fight.

yourWindow.when: His Blinding Dart (Q) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Step in and trade — your Q-empowered autos will actually land, and W (Haymaker) is always safe to throw since it isn't an attack. If a minion is sitting opposite him, this is also your window to land E (Facebreaker) for the stun instead of just a slow.

powerCurve.note: Blind + ranged poison poke outrange your engage tools
Q empowered autos and W shield start matching his poke
R (Show Stopper) adds a hard punish for overextensions
Stridebreaker + Sterak's let you tank poke and all-in

start.why: This is the dominant start on 78.6% of games for a reason: the flat damage reduction on minion/champion hits plus the regen offsets Toxic Shot's DoT and Blinding Dart's chip, letting you actually hold CS instead of backing off the wave.

boots.why: The 59.8%-pick, magic-resist choice directly answers Teemo's all-magic damage profile (poison, dart, mushroom clouds) and the tenacity shortens how long Noxious Trap's slow zones you in place.

core.why: The attack-speed burst and slow close the gap on a champion whose only defense once you're on him is W (Move Quick) kiting — this is the single highest-pick-rate first core item in the data.
Health plus damage-over-time sustain keeps you alive through extended poke phases before you're fully itemized.
The highest-win-rate full path (61.5% over 13 games) — the shield and tenacity let you walk through a blind-and-poke sequence without losing the trade.

situational.when: he leans on mushroom zoning to slow your approach through brush and river
the game goes long and you need armor shred to end trades before he escapes
you're ahead and want to pressure side lanes and objectives solo
you want faster cooldowns on Q and E to chain trades more often

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained stacking damage rewards the long poke-absorb-then-engage pattern this lane runs on, rather than a single burst window you won't get past his blind.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the highest win rate (52.4%) and by far the most-picked combo (64.6%) — Ignite converts your solo-kill edge into actual kills in the short trade windows his blind leaves open, since Teemo has no hard sustain to out-heal it.

playing.title: Farm behind minions, don't contest
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this lane is to keep distance and farm rather than fight — walk up for last hits only, then retreat before his Toxic Shot auto range (680) catches you again.

playing.title: Track his Q, trade on cooldown
playing.detail: Blinding Dart is 8 seconds — once it's spent on you or a minion, step in. Your Q-empowered punches will actually connect instead of being blinded.

playing.title: Stack minions for the stun
playing.detail: E (Facebreaker, 490 range) only stuns if enemies are on opposite sides of you; against a kiting Teemo with no minion behind him, it just slows — reposition so a minion sits opposite him before casting.

playing.title: Let W absorb poke, don't force it
playing.detail: Haymaker stores Grit from all damage you take, including poison ticks — let it build passively through his poke, then expend it for the shield and true-damage punch rather than casting it on cooldown.

playing.title: Respect fresh mushrooms near brush
playing.detail: Noxious Trap has essentially no cooldown (1s) — check tri-bush and jungle entrances for recently placed traps before diving or chasing, since the slow-and-DoT cloud can turn a chase into a death.

playing.title: Save R for isolated punishes
playing.detail: Show Stopper is 120/100/80 seconds — hold it for a moment he's out of position (after using Move Quick's sprint to reposition, or caught pushing too far), not as an opener.

playing.title: All-in once Stridebreaker completes
playing.detail: The slow-on-proc lets you actually stick to him through Move Quick's speed boost — this is the point the lane tips from even to clearly in your favor.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win rates/sample sizes above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the ability mechanics and tactical reasoning (blind interactions, stun setup, cooldown windows) are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Teemo punish you during early game by keeping your distance. Focus on farming and using [W] to poke while waiting for a chance when he steps in your range.
